source_1.title: Configuring reserved concurrency for a function
source_1.quote: You can reserve up to the Unreserved account concurrency value minus 100. The remaining 100 units of concurrency are for functions that aren't using reserved concurrency.

source_2.quote: You can reserve concurrency for as many functions as you like, as long as you leave at least 100 simultaneous executions unreserved for functions that aren't configured with a per-function limit.

source_3.finding: the CreateFunction request body does NOT contain ReservedConcurrentExecutions
source_3.quote: The other parameters let you configure version-specific and function-level settings ... Function-level settings apply to both the unpublished and published versions of the function, and include tags (TagResource) and per-function concurrency limits (PutFunctionConcurrency).

documented_rule.arithmetic: UnreservedConcurrentExecutions (10) - documented floor (100) = -90. No positive reservation is satisfiable on this account. Field reports on 10-ceiling accounts show the floor reported as [10] rather than [100]; both readings give the same answer, because the ceiling IS the floor.

correction_to_the_lead.lead_wrote: The expected outcome of the authorised apply is a failed CreateFunction, after the log group, role, policy and attachment have already been created.
correction_to_the_lead.measured: CreateFunction does not carry the parameter and will SUCCEED. The hashicorp/aws provider issues CreateFunction, waits for the function to become Active, and then issues a separate PutFunctionConcurrency, which is what fails.

empirical_check_on_the_pinned_provider.reading: the post-create PutFunctionConcurrency error wrapper is present in the exact provider build that would run the apply

correction_to_the_lead.provider_source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/main/internal/service/lambda/function.go — resourceFunctionCreate builds lambda.CreateFunctionInput without ReservedConcurrentExecutions, then calls conn.PutFunctionConcurrency after creation.

expected_failure.expected_terraform_error_shape: Error: setting Lambda Function (mainline-demo-api) concurrency: operation error Lambda: PutFunctionConcurrency, https response error StatusCode: 400, RequestID: <uuid>, InvalidParameterValueException: Specified ReservedConcurrentExecutions for function decreases account's UnreservedConcurrentExecution below its minimum value of [10].

created_before_the_failure.why: CreateFunction returns 201 and the provider calls d.SetId() BEFORE PutFunctionConcurrency; the function exists in AWS and is written to state as TAINTED

not_created.why: its alarm widget lists all four alarm ARNs (main.tf:598-603), so it depends on the alarms and transitively on the function

partial_apply_shape.one_mercy: the Function URL is NOT created, so the partial apply leaves nothing publicly reachable — the failure is a mess, not an exposure

candidates.cost_ceiling_change: none — min(20, account 10) = 10 either way; ap-southeast-1 holds 0 other functions
candidates.what_is_given_up: the module documents that Lambda emits per-function ConcurrentExecutions reliably only for functions that HAVE reserved concurrency, so the -concurrency alarm can sit in INSUFFICIENT_DATA (variables.tf:381-383, README.md:653-657). But that alarm is already unreachable: its threshold is > 20 and this account's ConcurrentExecutions can never exceed 10. Throttles is still emitted and still fires at the account ceiling, so the throttle tripwire survives.

candidates.why: 10 - 100 = -90; no value >= 1 satisfies the documented floor. reserved = 0 passes the API but the module's own validation message says it: 'Note that 0 disables the function entirely.'

scenario_a_judging_session.logs: 380 * ~1.5 KB = 0.57 MB, inside the 5 GB free ingest (confirmed active)

scenario_b_demo_health_hourly_cron_30_da.arithmetic: 720 * 10.6 s * 0.5 GB = 3816 GB-s; health 720 * 0.4 s * 0.5 GB = 144 GB-s; total 3960 GB-s over 1440 requests

scenario_c1_sustained_abuse_gate_run_flo.shape: 10 concurrent (the ACCOUNT ceiling) x 15 s per invocation x 512 MB, for 30 days

scenario_c1_sustained_abuse_gate_run_flo.note: the compute term is invariant in the reservation. min(20, 10) = 10 and min(-1 -> account pool, 10) = 10, so USD 167.47 is the compute ceiling whether reserved_concurrent_executions is 20, -1, or anything in between.

scenario_c2_sustained_abuse_egress_flood.shape: the same 10 concurrent, but fetching the 1,554,168-byte source map instead of running the gate. Compute is invariant (concurrency x wall-time x memory is fixed); requests/second and therefore egress are not.
scenario_c2_sustained_abuse_egress_flood.static_serve_latency_assumption: UNMEASURED — no function is deployed. Band 100-300 ms.
scenario_c2_sustained_abuse_egress_flood.reading: this, not the gate-run flood, is the worst case. Nothing in the plan bounds egress: no CloudFront (excluded by the account's verification hold), no WAF, no rate limit in the handler, no alarm on BytesOut, no budget action.

vendor_publishes_today.quote: Each pay-as-you-go CockroachDB Cloud organization is given $15 of resource consumption (equivalent to 50 million Request Units and 10 GiB of storage) for free each month.

free_allowance.discrepancy: the repo's 100 M RU is 2x the vendor's published 50 M. Unverified against the org's own Cloud Console, which is the only place that would settle it. Both figures are carried through the arithmetic below.

ru_accounting_formula.replication: writes are replicated to 3 storage processes by default and each replica is counted as a separate write operation

ru_per_gate_run_estimate.method: the published formula applied to the measured payload and the code path. NOT a metered reading.

reads.basis: 10 count(*) subqueries over a 27-row working set, plus the permit row and the site join

writes.basis: UPDATE mainline.permit, INSERT mainline.disposition, and the writes inside CALL mainline.merge_permit — all rolled back, but the intents are written and billed — each at 3 replicas and 1 KiB payload granularity

sql_cpu.basis: 1 RU per 3 ms SQL CPU. Wall is 10,642.9 ms but that includes ~90 ms RTT per statement from a developer machine in Australia. At 3-10 % of wall as SQL CPU, 0.32-1.06 s, this is the dominant term.

ru_per_gate_run_estimate.what_would_settle_it: one reading of the RU chart in the CockroachDB Cloud Console, or the Cloud API's usage endpoint. Nobody has taken it. This estimate should not be quoted as measured.

exhaustion_under_sustained_abuse.rate_bound: the AWS concurrency ceiling of 10, divided by the measured 10.6 s gate run = 0.943 gate runs/s = 81,510 per day

at_300_ru_central.arithmetic: 50 M free + (USD 25.00 / USD 0.20 per M) = 50 M + 125 M = 175 M RU

exhaustion_under_sustained_abuse.conclusion: the cluster is disabled somewhere between day 4 and day 14 of a sustained flood; most likely around day 7

what_the_judges_see_when_it_is_exhausted.the_bill_does_not_stop: the CockroachDB spend limit stops the database, not the Lambda. AWS keeps metering at USD 167.47 per 30 days while every request returns a 500.
